task_instance: Scaffold Better Auth email/password authentication into a minimal Express + TypeScript sample app: create auth.ts with a better-sqlite3 database and emailAndPassword enabled, generate BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and set BETTER_AUTH_URL, run the Better Auth CLI migration to create the schema, mount the Node route handler, verify the health endpoint, and perform a real email/password sign-up.
evidence: Node v22.22.0 / npm 10.9.4 available. In the work directory: created package.json (ESM), installed better-auth@1.7.14, express@5.3.0, better-sqlite3, and @better-auth/cli locally into ./node_modules (no global, no sudo); better-sqlite3 native module verified working via a node select-1 query. Generated a 44-char base64 BETTER_AUTH_SECRET with node crypto and wrote .env with secret and base URL. Wrote auth.ts (betterAuth with new Database('sqlite.db'), emailAndPassword.enabled, exported Session type). Ran the bundled Better Auth CLI migrate (./node_modules/.bin/better-auth migrate): it reported the four missing tables, applied the schema, and printed 'migration was completed successfully'. Confirmed sqlite.db now contains tables account, session, user, verification. Mounted the handler in Express via toNodeHandler(auth) using the Express 5 named-wildcard route /api/auth/{*any} (the skill's Express-4-style /api/auth/* pattern throws under path-to-regexp v8 in Express 5; adjusting the wildcard is a framework-version fix, not a skill replacement). GET /api/auth/ok returned HTTP 200 with body {"ok":true} (current better-auth health response; the skill text's {status:'ok'} is an outdated body but the ok endpoint works). Then exercised the core deliverable end to end: POST to the email sign-up endpoint with a matching Origin header returned HTTP 200 with a session token and user object, and the SQLite DB persisted the new user row plus a 'credential' provider account row. Files produced: auth.ts, server.ts, run_and_test.mjs, signup_test.mjs, .env, sqlite.db, package.json, node_modules/ (all under the work directory). Verified = migration created real schema, health endpoint 200, and a real sign-up created and persisted a user.
